title: Raspberry Pi Temperature and Throttling
dataSources: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`).
app: Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=rpi:metric
| stats max(cpu_temp_c) as peak_temp, sum(eval(throttled=1)) as throttle_events by host
| where peak_temp>80 OR throttle_events>0
| sort - peak_temp
description: Watches your Raspberry Pis for overheating and CPU throttling, the usual culprit behind a sluggish or crashing Pi project.
value: A throttling Pi is slow for a reason you cannot see in the app; surfacing temperature and throttling points at a fan or heatsink fix.
implementation: Forward Pi temperature and throttle flags; schedule every few minutes and alert on overheating.
visualization: Table of Pis by peak temperature and throttle-event count.
grandmaExplanation: It watches your little home-project computers for overheating, which is usually why they get slow or crash.
